author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can view a read-only specialty directory listing every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page at GET /specialties.html names every stored specialty and, under each, the veterinarians who hold it by full name (first name before last). It lists specialties, not the full vet roster; a vet with no specialty is absent. All specialties render on one page without pagination. Reachable by address only, no navigation entry.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html returns a page naming every stored specialty, each with the veterinarians who hold it, all on one page with no pagination
Each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown by full name with the first name before the last (for example 'Helen Leary')
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
A stored specialty that no veterinarian holds is still named, shown with no veterinarians under it
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable non-arbitrary order
When no specialties are stored, the page renders as an empty directory rather than failing
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2)
A navigation entry or link to the page from anywhere else (deferred, possible follow-up)
notes: New requirement minted this dispatch; inverts REQ-VET-001's axis (specialties-with-vets vs vets-with-specialties) on a separate page /specialties.html, so no contradiction. REQ-SYS-001 governs nav TO owner/vet areas and is not contradicted by this page carrying no inbound link. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md: sort key for specialties/vets, whether an unheld specialty should show or hide, and whether a visible entry point is a follow-up. file_targets and test_names best-effort; system-design may introduce a dedicated SpecialtyController/SpecialtyRepository.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged as a small extension of existing patterns. The specialty directory reuses the controller-depends-on-repository shape (system-design.md#contracts): a new SpecialtyRepository mirrors PetTypeRepository's name-ordered findAll, a new unpaged GetMapping on VetController mirrors showVetList minus pagination, and a new Thymeleaf template mirrors vets/vetList.html. The only genuinely new logic is inverting the unidirectional Vet->Specialty association in-memory, which the invariants note added to system-design.md#contracts now records. No new module, pattern, or integration boundary; NG-2 (read-only) is preserved.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html on VetController returns view vets/specialtyList with a model attribute (recommend LinkedHashMap<Specialty,List<Vet>> in specialty-name order, or an equivalent typed list/record) carrying every specialty with the veterinarians holding it.

New SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty,Integer> exposing a name-ordered findAll (JPQL ORDER BY name, mirroring PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes); it is the authoritative source that keeps an unheld specialty on the page.
Read path reuses VetRepository.findAll() (already @Cacheable, EAGER-fetches specialties) for the vets side; no new query on the vet side is needed because Specialty has no back-reference to Vet.
Template renders each veterinarian's full name as firstName + ' ' + lastName, reusing the exact expression from vetList.html line 18.

patterns.description: declarative name-ordered findAll via explicit @Query ORDER BY name — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies
controller-builds-model-and-returns-view-name pattern the new showSpecialtyList method follows, without the pagination helper

risks.risk: Grouping by Specialty object identity fails: SpecialtyRepository.findAll() and VetRepository.findAll() run as separate reads and BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so a vet's Specialty instances need not be the same objects as the directory's. contains()/keying by reference would silently drop veterinarians.
risks.mitigation: Invert by identity VALUE — group vets under each directory specialty by specialty id (or unique name), not by object reference. Recorded as an invariant in system-design.md#contracts.

risks.risk: Edge cases (unheld specialty appears; vet with no specialty absent; zero specialties) are not exercisable from H2 seed data, where all three seeded specialties are held.
risks.mitigation: VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest with @MockitoBean repositories (see existing setup); the implementer constructs an unheld Specialty and a specialty-less Vet directly, as the current tests already build Vet fixtures. Assert on the model attribute and rendered content.

risks.risk: Adding tests to VetControllerTests inherits its @MockitoBean setup, which sits in tension with CLAUDE.md's no-mocks testing policy.
risks.mitigation: Pre-existing tension not introduced by this slice (VetControllerTests already mocks VetRepository); leave the resolution to test-reviewer/testing-principles rather than diverging the new tests from the file's established pattern.

notes: ADR explicitly NOT warranted: no hard-to-reverse or surprising decision. The one design choice — invert the association in-memory in the controller rather than add a bidirectional ManyToMany on the Vet aggregate or a Specialty-side query — is low-stakes, easily reversible, and driven by the existing unidirectional mapping; it is captured as current-state in system-design.md#contracts, not as a rationale ADR. Controller placement: the new route is added to VetController (per prd-entry file_targets) rather than a dedicated SpecialtyController, matching the vet feature's single-controller grain; a separate controller was considered and rejected as it would fragment the feature package for no behavioural gain. Open PRD questions are satisfied by narrowest-reading defaults already recorded: specialties sorted by name and vets by name give the required stable order; the unheld specialty is named (SpecialtyRepository is authoritative). system-design.md updated: SpecialtyRepository contract row added, VetController/Vet/Specialty Implements wired to REQ-VET-003, and one invariant sentence on the unidirectional-association inversion. No design-doc-autofix records present; autofix audit skipped.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 3 has no test: 'When the clinic stores no specialties, the page renders as an empty directory rather than failing.' No test stubs specialties.findAll() to return an empty list and verifies the controller returns 200 with an empty model rather than throwing. A NullPointerException or iteration failure on an empty collection would go undetected.

Mocking-policy explicit call: extending @MockitoBean to SpecialtyRepository is out-of-policy for new code. The brief's tolerance clause ('the existing suite stubs collaborators with a mock framework, and that usage may stay') covers the pre-existing @MockitoBean VetRepository but not new stubs. For new code the brief requires 'a real implementation or a hand-written double first; a framework stub is a conscious exception, chosen only when neither fits.' A real Spring Data JPA implementation fits: a @SpringBootTest + H2 integration test class covering the six specialty-directory behaviors is the policy-compliant path.

All six new test methods violate the BDD naming school ('the{Subject}Should{Outcome}') mandated for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. Current names (showSpecialtyListHtml, specialtyListRendersAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, etc.) name the action called rather than the observable outcome. Suggested renames: showSpecialtyListHtml -> theSpecialtyListShouldRespondOkWithSpecialtiesModel; specialtyListRendersAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage -> theSpecialtyListShouldContainEveryStoredSpecialtyOnOnePage; specialtyListNamesSpecialtyHeldByNoVet -> theSpecialtyListShouldIncludeSpecialtiesHeldByNoVet; specialtyListShowsVetsByFullName -> theSpecialtyListShouldShowVetsByFirstNameThenLastName; specialtyListOmitsVetWithoutSpecialty -> theSpecialtyListShouldOmitVetsHoldingNoSpecialty; specialtyListGroupsVetsByIdentityValueNotReference -> theSpecialtyListShouldGroupVetsBySpecialtyIdNotObjectReference.
findings.fix: Rename all six methods to the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form per docs/testing-principles.md § Test Naming.

findings.description: Two tests use org.hamcrest.Matchers (containsString, not) inside MockMvc content().string() instead of AssertJ. The brief requires fluent AssertJ assertions. Class sweep: only these two sites use org.hamcrest.Matchers directly in the diff.

approved_aspects: Done-when criteria 1-3 all covered: showSpecialtyListHtml (200 + model attr + view name), specialtyListShowsVetsByFullName (first-before-last), specialtyListOmitsVetWithoutSpecialty (absent from page)
PRD edge cases 1 (unheld specialty present) and 2 (stable order via containsExactly) are covered

specialtyListGroupsVetsByIdentityValueNotReference is a precise guard for the BaseEntity no-equals/hashCode invariant documented in system-design.md; distinct Specialty instances in @BeforeEach make the test meaningful
Factory methods specialty(), james(), helen() comply with the brief's construction policy
AssertJ used correctly for all model-level assertions (extracting, containsExactly, isEmpty, noneMatch)
All six new tests pass; build is green

A reader encounters `held by` on one line and `// no` on the next, forcing a stop-and-reparse to reconstruct the sentence. Same defect appears in `VetControllerTests.java:92` (`// and`). All five instances are in code introduced by this change.
findings.fix: Rewrite the two comment blocks in `showSpecialtyList` (lines 76–87) and the one comment in `setup()` (lines 91–93) as correctly wrapped prose so that no `//` line holds a single word. The content is correct; only the word-wrapping needs fixing.

findings.description: Two assertions use fully qualified `org.hamcrest.Matchers.containsString(...)` and `org.hamcrest.Matchers.not(org.hamcrest.Matchers.containsString(...))` inline. The rest of the test class relies on static imports, making the qualification inconsistent and harder to read at a glance.
findings.fix: Add `import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.containsString;` and `import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.not;` and replace the two inline qualified references with the unqualified names.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: Three sentences in the new documentation exceed the 30-word writing-standards limit. (1) docs/prd.md narrative paragraph, sentence beginning 'One page names every specialty the clinic stores…' (~44 words). (2) Same paragraph, sentence beginning 'The page is reached by its own address;…' (~40 words). (3) docs/system-design.md Invariants paragraph, the new sentence beginning 'The Vet→Specialty association is unidirectional…' (~62 words). All three are in the same class (sentence length); class sweep found no further instances in the diff. Autofix bounds exceeded for all three (replacement text >200 chars), so each must be split manually.

The new invariant sentence closes with an inline rationale clause: '…matching each vet's specialties to a directory specialty by identity value rather than object reference, since the two reads need not return the same Specialty instances.' The 'since' sub-clause explains the reason for the identity-value approach rather than asserting the invariant as fact. Per the document-writing prohibited pattern ('Why explanations in system-design.md → Critical → Create ADR; system-design.md carries only the rule plus an ADR back-link'), this needs resolution. The design-block (handoff.jsonl line 8) explicitly notes no ADR is warranted for this decision. System-design-expert should either (a) reword the clause as a factual invariant statement, removing the causal explanation (e.g., 'the two reads are independent and need not return the same Specialty instances, so the inversion uses identity value'), or (b) confirm the brief technical constraint is consistent with the existing invariants paragraph's established style and does not require a separate ADR link.
